chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام, when a matter grieved him, would wear two of his roughest and coarsest garments, then perform two rakʿahs in the latter part of the night.

Then, when he was in the last sajdah of his prostration, he would glorify Allah one hundred tasbihs, praise Allah one hundred times, declare the oneness of Allah one hundred times, and magnify Allah one hundred times.

Then he would acknowledge all of his sins: whatever of them he knew, he would confess to Him, Blessed and Exalted, during his prostration; and whatever of them he did not remember, he would acknowledge collectively. Then he would supplicate to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and press his knees to the ground.

key_terms.هَلَّلَ: he declared divine oneness by saying tahlil

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام pray and make du'a when he was troubled by a matter?
ai.summary: This report describes the devotional practice of Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام when afflicted by distress. It highlights night salat, abundant dhikr, confession of sins, and earnest du'a as a model of humility and turning to Allah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1545 - When Ali ibn al-Hussain (as) was troubled by a matter, he would wear two of his roughest and coarsest garments, then stand for two units of prayer in the last part of the night.

When he reached the last prostration (Sujood), he would glorify Allah (swt) one hundred times, praise Allah (swt) one hundred times, declare the oneness of Allah (swt) (La ilaha illAllah (swt)) one hundred times, and magnify Allah (swt) (Allahu Akbar) one hundred times.

Then, he would acknowledge all of his sins — everything he remembered, he would confess before Allah (swt), the Blessed and Exalted, during his prostration; what he could not recall, he would acknowledge in general. Thereafter, he would supplicate to Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, while placing his knees on the ground.
